metadata.scenario: A caller urgently requests advice on managing severe swelling post-surgery. Category: Urgent Request. Flags: urgent_request.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Lucille Davis. I'm really concerned about my swelling. Hi Lucille, it’s good to hear from you, but I'm sorry to hear about the swelling. Can you tell me more about it? Yes, I had surgery three days ago, and the swelling has gotten quite severe. What should I do? That sounds uncomfortable. Have you had any fever or increased pain? No fever, but the pain is definitely worsening. I understand. It’s important to manage that swelling. Have you been elevating your leg? Yes, I’ve been trying to keep it up, but it doesn’t seem to help much. Elevation is key, but we may need to assess the swelling further. Would you like me to send a nurse for an evaluation? Yes, please! That would be great. I just want to make sure it's not something serious. Let me check the schedule. We have a nurse available tomorrow afternoon. Would that work for you? Yes, that works for me. Thank you! Perfect! I’ll arrange for Robert, our registered nurse, to visit you then. Is there anything else I should be doing in the meantime? Yes, you should continue to ice the area for 15 to 20 minutes every couple of hours. Okay, I can do that. Great! I’ll also follow up with you after the visit to see how you're feeling. Thank you, Margaret. That means a lot. Of course! And if the swelling worsens or you notice any red flags like fever, call us immediately. Will do. I really appreciate your help. It’s my pleasure, Lucille. By the way, if you're feeling overwhelmed, we also offer personal care assistance. I’ve had that before; it helped a lot! I can arrange that again for you if needed. Just let me know. Sounds good. I’ll think about it. Thank you for calling, Lucille. Take care and I’ll speak to you soon! Bye, Margaret!
